question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Ravi and Kabir are twins, (a)/ but Ravi is the tallest (b)/ and the more (c)/ athletic of the two. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When two persons or things are compared, the comparative degree is used with "the" and "of the two" — "the taller … of the two". The superlative "the tallest" is used only for three or more. Part (c) already uses the comparative "the more", so the sentence also needs "the taller" to stay consistent.

◦ Corrected sentence: Ravi and Kabir are twins, but Ravi is the taller and the more athletic of the two.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Ravi and Kabir are twins," is a proper clause, with the plural verb "are" agreeing with the compound subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "and the more" is a proper comparative that matches "of the two".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "athletic of the two." correctly completes the comparative with "of the two".

 

NOTE

 

• Of the two brothers, Anil is the elder but Of the three brothers, Anil is the eldest. Comparative + "of the two" takes "the": the better of the two, the cheaper of the two.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The visiting team (a)/ struggled in the first half (b)/ but played very good (c)/ after the interval. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Good" is an adjective, and it describes a noun. The verb "played" must be described by an adverb, and the adverb form of "good" is "well". So "played very good" must be "played very well".

◦ Corrected sentence: The visiting team struggled in the first half but played very well after the interval.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The visiting team" is a proper singular collective subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "struggled in the first half" is a proper past verb phrase with a prepositional phrase of time.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "after the interval." is a proper prepositional phrase of time.

 

NOTE

 

• good (adjective) – well (adverb): She is a good singer, She sings well. "Well" is also an adjective meaning "healthy": I am quite well now.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

The new stadium is twice bigger than the old one in seating capacity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. twice as big as.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Multiples such as twice, thrice, half, three times are expressed with the positive degree in the pattern "multiplier + as + adjective + as". So "twice bigger than" must be "twice as big as".

◦ Corrected sentence: The new stadium is twice as big as the old one in seating capacity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "twice as bigger as" — "as … as" needs the positive degree "big", and "bigger" is a comparative.

 

• Option 3: "as twice big as" — the word order is wrong; the multiplier must come before the first "as".

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because a multiple is not combined with a comparative and "than" in standard usage.

 

NOTE

 

• twice as long as, half as much as, three times as large as, ten times as fast as. Rule: multiplier before the first "as".

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The layout of the new library (a)/ is similar with (b)/ that of the old one. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The adjective "similar" is followed by the preposition "to", and not by "with". So "similar with" must be "similar to".

◦ Corrected sentence: The layout of the new library is similar to that of the old one.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The layout of the new library" is a proper singular subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "that of the old one" correctly compares like with like, since "that" stands for "the layout".

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "similar with" in part (b) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• Adjective + preposition: similar to, equal to, superior to, senior to, junior to but different from, identical with, the same as.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Before the next class, (a)/ the teacher asked us (b)/ to summarise (c)/ the two first chapters. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When an ordinal (first, second, last, next) and a cardinal (one, two, three) are used together before a noun, the ordinal comes first. So "the two first chapters" must be "the first two chapters".

◦ Corrected sentence: Before the next class, the teacher asked us to summarise the first two chapters.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Before the next class," is a proper introductory prepositional phrase of time.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the teacher asked us" is a proper subject and verb in the simple past.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "to summarise" is a proper infinitive that follows "asked us".

 

NOTE

 

• the first two chapters, the last three days, the next five years — never the two first, the three last, the five next.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

After years of city life, it took her a long time to become accustomed to ___ in a small village.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. living.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In "accustomed to" (also used to in the sense of "familiar with", addicted to, devoted to, committed to), the word "to" is a preposition, not the infinitive marker. A preposition is followed by a noun or a gerund (-ing form), so the correct word is "living".

◦ Complete sentence: After years of city life, it took her a long time to become accustomed to living in a small village.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "live" — this treats "to" as an infinitive marker, which is wrong after "accustomed".

 

• Option 2: "have lived" — this is a perfect infinitive, and it also treats "to" as an infinitive marker.

 

• Option 4: "be living" — this is a continuous infinitive, and again it does not follow the preposition "to".

 

NOTE

 

• accustomed to living, look forward to meeting, object to paying (preposition + gerund) but used to live (past habit, base verb): She used to live in Delhi.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

There is not some (a)/ vacancy in the hotel (b)/ at the moment, (c)/ so please try elsewhere. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Some" is used in affirmative sentences, and "any" is used in negative sentences and questions. So "not some vacancy" must be "not any vacancy" (or "no vacancy").

◦ Corrected sentence: There is not any vacancy in the hotel at the moment, so please try elsewhere.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "vacancy in the hotel" is a proper noun phrase with a correct preposition.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "at the moment," is a proper adverbial phrase of time.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "so please try elsewhere." is a proper clause of result with an imperative.

 

NOTE

 

• I have some doubts but I do not have any doubts; Is there any milk?; If you need any help, call me. "Some" is kept in offers and requests: Would you like some tea?.

question: Select the sentence that is grammatically correct.
option_1: Rohit is more taller than his cousin by three inches.
option_2: This medicine is more preferable than that one.
option_3: I have read the both novels recommended by the teacher.
option_4: Our elder daughter is studying medicine in Pune.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Our elder daughter is studying medicine in Pune.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Only Option 4 is correct. "Elder" is used for members of a family when two are compared or when one of two is meant, and it is placed before the noun — "our elder daughter".

◦ Correct sentence: Our elder daughter is studying medicine in Pune.

 

• Each of the other three options contains a different adjective error, explained below.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "more taller than" — "taller" is already a comparative, so "more" makes it a double comparative: "Rohit is taller than his cousin".

 

• Option 2: "more preferable than" — "preferable" is already comparative in sense and takes "to"; it cannot take "more" or "than": "This medicine is preferable to that one".

 

• Option 3: "the both novels" — the words both, all, half come before the article: "both the novels".

 

NOTE

 

• elder brother / elder sister (before a noun, family only) but older than for comparisons; both the boys, all the students, half the time (predeterminer + article); preferable to, superior to; never a double comparative: more taller, more better.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The receptionist (a)/ spoke to us very friendly (b)/ and offered us tea (c)/ while we waited. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Friendly" ends in "-ly" but it is an adjective, and it has no adverb form. Such words are turned into an adverbial phrase with "in a … manner / way". So "spoke to us very friendly" must be "spoke to us in a very friendly manner".

◦ Corrected sentence: The receptionist spoke to us in a very friendly manner and offered us tea while we waited.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The receptionist" is a proper singular subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "and offered us tea" is a proper coordinate verb phrase with two objects.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "while we waited." is a proper clause of time in the simple past.

 

NOTE

 

• Adjectives ending in -ly: friendly, lovely, lonely, likely, costly, lively, silly, cowardly, elderly, deadly. They cannot modify verbs: use in a friendly way / in a cowardly fashion.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The question paper was very lengthy, (a)/ and the last section was (b)/ too difficult that (c)/ hardly any student could attempt it. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The result clause with "that" needs the structure "so + adjective + that". "Too" is used with the infinitive — "too + adjective + to". So "too difficult that" must be "so difficult that".

◦ Corrected sentence: The question paper was very lengthy, and the last section was so difficult that hardly any student could attempt it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The question paper was very lengthy," is a proper clause, with "very" correctly used before a positive adjective.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "and the last section was" is a proper coordinate clause with a singular subject and verb.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "hardly any student could attempt it." is a proper result clause, and "hardly any" is followed by a singular noun.

 

NOTE

 

• so difficult that nobody could solve it (result); too difficult to solve (negative result); such a difficult paper that…. The three patterns cannot be mixed: too … that is wrong.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Almost students (a)/ of the senior class (b)/ have cleared (c)/ the qualifying test. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Almost" is an adverb (= nearly) and cannot be used directly before a noun. The determiner that means "the majority of" is "most". So "Almost students" must be "Most students" (or "Almost all the students").

◦ Corrected sentence: Most students of the senior class have cleared the qualifying test.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "of the senior class" is a proper prepositional phrase that names the group.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "have cleared" is a proper present perfect verb, and the plural verb agrees with "students".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "the qualifying test." is a proper noun phrase, with "qualifying" used as an adjective.

 

NOTE

 

• most students / most of the students but almost all the students / almost every student / almost everyone. Never almost students or almost people.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The coach's ___ advice during the final over helped the team win the match.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. invaluable.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Invaluable" does not mean "not valuable". The prefix "in-" here gives the sense of "beyond", so the word means extremely valuable, priceless. Advice that helped the team win is therefore "invaluable".

◦ Complete sentence: The coach's invaluable advice during the final over helped the team win the match.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "valueless" — this means having no worth, which is the opposite of what the sentence needs.

 

• Option 2: "unvalued" — this means not appreciated or not given any value, so it does not fit advice that helped win a match.

 

• Option 3: "invaluably" — this is an adverb, and an adjective is needed before the noun "advice".

 

NOTE

 

• invaluable (priceless) — an invaluable asset; valuable (worth a lot); valueless / worthless (no worth). Similar traps: flammable = inflammable (both "easily set on fire").

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Ravi is (a)/ so a talented batsman (b)/ that every club (c)/ wants to sign him. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• After "so", the adjective comes before the article: "so + adjective + a + noun". The alternative is "such + a + adjective + noun". So "so a talented batsman" must be "so talented a batsman" (or "such a talented batsman").

◦ Corrected sentence: Ravi is so talented a batsman that every club wants to sign him.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Ravi is" is a proper singular subject and verb.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "that every club" is a proper result clause, and "every" is followed by a singular noun.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "wants to sign him." is a proper verb phrase, and "wants" agrees with "every club".

 

NOTE

 

• so beautiful a day = such a beautiful day; the same order follows "as, how, too": as good a player, too heavy a load, how long a journey.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The architect (a)/ has designed (b)/ an unique building for the campus. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the sound of the next word, not on its spelling. "Unique" begins with the consonant sound /j/ (as in "you"), so it takes "a": "a unique building".

◦ Corrected sentence: The architect has designed a unique building for the campus.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The architect" is a proper singular subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "has designed" is a proper present perfect verb phrase.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "an unique" in part (c) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• a university, a European, a one-day match, a useful tool, a uniform (consonant sound /j/ or /w/) but an hour, an honest man, an heir, an MLA (vowel sound).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

A human treatment of the prisoners (a)/ is what the activists (b)/ have been demanding (c)/ for several years. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Human" means "relating to people", while "humane" means "kind, compassionate and showing mercy". Treatment that is kind and merciful is "humane treatment".

◦ Corrected sentence: A humane treatment of the prisoners is what the activists have been demanding for several years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "is what the activists" is proper, and the singular verb "is" agrees with the singular subject "treatment".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "have been demanding" is a proper present perfect continuous verb that agrees with "activists".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "for several years." is a proper prepositional phrase of duration, used correctly with the perfect continuous.

 

NOTE

 

• human (of people) — human rights, human nature; humane (kind) — a humane society, a humane method. Similar pairs: childish (immature) / childlike (innocent), ingenious (clever) / ingenuous (naive).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

 

The referee showed a yellow card to ___ of the two players.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. each.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Each" is a distributive word that refers to the members of a group one by one, and it can be used for two or more persons, followed by "of the two". "Every" is never followed by "of", and it is used only for a group of more than two.

◦ Complete sentence: The referee showed a yellow card to each of the two players.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "any" — "any of the two" does not give the sense of both players being booked; for two persons the distributive words are "each" and "either".

 

• Option 2: "every" — "every" cannot be followed by "of the two" and is used for more than two.

 

• Option 3: "all" — "all" is used for more than two persons; for two, the word is "both".

 

NOTE

 

• For two: each / either / both / neither; for more than two: every / all / any / none. each of the two players, either of the two, both the players.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The manager appears to be a capable man, (a)/ but he seems quite indifferent for (b)/ the staff's problems (c)/ and rarely listens. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The adjective "indifferent" is followed by the preposition "to". So "indifferent for" must be "indifferent to".

◦ Corrected sentence: The manager appears to be a capable man, but he seems quite indifferent to the staff's problems and rarely listens.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "appears to be a capable man," is a proper clause, and "appears" agrees with the singular subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "the staff's problems" is a proper noun phrase with a correct possessive.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "and rarely listens." is a proper coordinate verb phrase, and the adverb "rarely" correctly comes before the verb.

 

NOTE

 

• Adjective + preposition: indifferent to, capable of, fond of, jealous of, proud of, ashamed of, aware of, conscious of, sceptical about, keen on, good at, responsible for, famous for, angry with (a person) / at (a thing).

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

Sheela is most intelligent girl in her class.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. the most intelligent girl.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A superlative used to compare one person with all the others in a group must be preceded by "the". So "most intelligent girl in her class" must be "the most intelligent girl in her class".

◦ Corrected sentence: Sheela is the most intelligent girl in her class.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "more intelligent girl" — this is a comparative and needs "than" or "the … of the two"; it does not compare Sheela with the whole class.

 

• Option 2: "most intelligent girls" — the plural noun does not agree with the single subject "Sheela".

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because the article "the" is missing before the superlative.

 

NOTE

 

• the best, the tallest, the most beautiful. Without "the", "most" means "very": a most enjoyable evening (= very enjoyable) or "the majority": most people.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The candidates studied hardly (a)/ for the entrance test (b)/ throughout the year, (c)/ yet several of them failed. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Hard" is both an adjective and an adverb, meaning "with great effort". "Hardly" is a different adverb meaning "scarcely, almost not". The sense here is "with great effort", so "studied hardly" must be "studied hard".

◦ Corrected sentence: The candidates studied hard for the entrance test throughout the year, yet several of them failed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "for the entrance test" is a proper prepositional phrase of purpose.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "throughout the year," is a proper prepositional phrase of duration.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "yet several of them failed." is a proper clause of contrast, and "several of them" takes a plural verb.

 

NOTE

 

• Adverbs with two forms and different meanings: hard (with effort) / hardly (scarcely); late (not on time) / lately (recently); near (close) / nearly (almost); high (upward) / highly (very); wide (fully) / widely (commonly).

question: Select the sentence in which the underlined word is used incorrectly.
option_1: The team won three successive matches in the league.
option_2: She is a practical person who avoids unrealistic plans.
option_3: The scheme is not practicable without additional funds.
option_4: The luxuriant hotel offered a spa and a private pool.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The luxuriant hotel offered a spa and a private pool.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In Option 4, "luxuriant" (growing thickly and richly, as in luxuriant hair or luxuriant vegetation) is the wrong word. A hotel that is expensive and very comfortable is "luxurious".

◦ Corrected sentence: The luxurious hotel offered a spa and a private pool.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 is correct — "successive" means following one after another, so "three successive matches" is properly used.

 

• Option 2 is correct — "practical" means sensible and concerned with actual results, so "a practical person" is properly used.

 

• Option 3 is correct — "practicable" means capable of being carried out, so "not practicable without additional funds" is properly used.

 

NOTE

 

• Confusable adjectives: successive / successful; practical / practicable; luxuriant / luxurious; comprehensive / comprehensible; eligible / legible; sociable / social.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The museum (a)/ is worth to visit (b)/ for anyone (c)/ interested in history. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The adjective "worth" is followed by a noun or a gerund (-ing form), and never by an infinitive. So "worth to visit" must be "worth visiting".

◦ Corrected sentence: The museum is worth visiting for anyone interested in history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The museum" is a proper singular subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "for anyone" is a proper prepositional phrase that names the person concerned.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "interested in history." is a proper participial phrase with the correct preposition.

 

NOTE

 

• worth reading, worth trying, worth a visit (gerund or noun) but worthy of attention. The related word worthwhile can take either form: It is worthwhile to visit / visiting the museum.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

The legal document was written in such complex language that it was hardly comprehensive to ordinary citizens.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. comprehensible.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Comprehensible" means "capable of being understood", while "comprehensive" means "complete and including everything". Language that ordinary citizens cannot follow is not "comprehensible to" them.

◦ Corrected sentence: The legal document was written in such complex language that it was hardly comprehensible to ordinary citizens.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "comprehending" — this describes the one who understands, and the document cannot "comprehend" anything.

 

• Option 3: "comprehended" — this is a past participle, which would need "by" and not "to".

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because "comprehensive" means complete and does not fit "to ordinary citizens".

 

NOTE

 

• a comprehensive report (complete) but a comprehensible explanation (understandable); incomprehensible (impossible to understand). Adjective + "to": comprehensible to, clear to, obvious to, familiar to.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

No other river in (a)/ India is as (b)/ sacred than (c)/ the Ganga. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the positive degree, the comparison is made with the pattern "as … as" (or "so … as" in negative statements). It is never followed by "than". So "as sacred than" must be "as sacred as".

◦ Corrected sentence: No other river in India is as sacred as the Ganga.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "No other river in" is a proper subject phrase, and "No other" is followed by a singular noun.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "India is as" is proper, since the first "as" correctly begins the positive comparison.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "the Ganga." is a proper object of the comparison.

 

NOTE

 

• The same idea in three degrees — positive: No other river is as sacred as the Ganga; comparative: The Ganga is more sacred than any other river; superlative: The Ganga is the most sacred river.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

Shady trees line the road (a)/ on either side (b)/ all along the way. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. "Either" as an adjective means "each of two" and is followed by a singular noun. So "on either side" is correct and means "on both sides". The form "either sides" would be wrong.

◦ Sentence as given: Shady trees line the road on either side all along the way.

 

• "Line" is correctly used as a verb meaning "to stand in a row along", and "all along the way" is a proper adverbial phrase of place.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Shady trees line the road" is a proper plural subject with the correct plural verb "line".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "on either side" correctly uses "either" with a singular noun.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "all along the way." is a proper adverbial phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• Do not over-correct: on either side = on both sides; in either hand, either way, neither side — "either" and "neither" take a singular noun.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The doctors are happy (a)/ that the patient (b)/ is responding well and looks (c)/ very better than yesterday. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Very" is used with the positive degree and the superlative ("the very best"), but never with a comparative. A comparative is strengthened by "much, far, a lot, still, even". So "very better" must be "much better".

◦ Corrected sentence: The doctors are happy that the patient is responding well and looks much better than yesterday.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The doctors are happy" is a proper plural subject with the correct plural verb.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "that the patient" is a proper noun clause opener with a singular subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "is responding well and looks" is proper, since "well" modifies the action "responding" and "looks" is a linking verb.

 

NOTE

 

• much better, far better, a lot better but very good (positive) and the very best (superlative). Never very better, very more, very taller.
